entities.name: Wenceslaus III of Bohemia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Wenceslaus III (born c. 1289 – died August 12, 1306) presided over the precipitous decline of the Přemyslid dynasty, a royal house that had ruled Bohemia since the 9th century. His brief and tumultuous reign, spanning from his ascension to the Hungarian throne in 1301 to his assassination in Olomouc in 1306, marked a pivotal moment in Central European dynastic politics, as he simultaneously held the crowns of Hungary, Bohemia, and Poland, albeit often tenuously. His personal ambition and his father Wenceslaus II's expansive foreign policy positioned him at the heart of a struggle for regional hegemony against the rising power of the Habsburgs and the influence of the Papacy.

Wenceslaus inherited the Hungarian crown in 1301 from his maternal grandfather, Andrew III, through a contested claim, taking the name Ladislaus V. However, his authority in Hungary was never fully established, challenged by Charles Robert of Anjou, and he eventually ceded his claim to Otto III of Bavaria in 1305. Upon his father Wenceslaus II's death in 1305, he became King of Bohemia and Poland, inheriting a more stable but still complex realm. His Polish claim, also inherited from his father, was fiercely contested by Władysław I Łokietek, leading Wenceslaus III to launch a military campaign into Poland in 1306, a venture cut short by his untimely death.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Wenceslaus III's death marked the violent end of the Přemyslid dynasty, directly leading to a major succession crisis in Bohemia and enabling the rise of the Luxembourg dynasty, fundamentally altering the political landscape of Central Europe.
